title: A wrapper flag typed at a command-level gate is passed to the tool as an argument, and the gate ignores it
body:
**A wrapper flag -- `--purge`, `--purge-only`, `--allow-empty` -- typed at a command-level gate is handed to the tool as an argument, and the gate does not do what was asked. No warning, no refusal.**

## Measured

One fixture project declaring the same `run: echo hello` twice, once as a gated option and once as a gated command (2026-09-17, vc, reviewing 0085):

- `devbin probe gated --purge` -- tool argv is `echo hello`, and the run reports `purged 0 old run file(s) ... keeping the newest 5`. Correct.
- `devbin sealed --purge` -- tool argv is `echo hello --purge`, the run prints `hello --purge`, and no purge happens.

`--purge-only` and `--allow-empty` take the same path. `--allow-empty` matters most: it is the corpus's explicit per-invocation "this emptiness is intended" override, so at a command-level gate an operator asking for it gets neither the override nor a refusal -- a corrupted command line and a gate that still fails.

## Not a new class: the defect gate_split_args was written to end, at a site added afterwards

`gate_split_args` (lib/runlog) exists because "`test mix --purge` asked mix to run a file called --purge", and its header claims "ONE parser, used by BOTH gate call sites ... so the two paths cannot drift on what counts as a wrapper flag."

There are THREE gate sites that take user argv. `gate_split_args` is called at `lib/gatecmd:100` and `lib/resolve:771`; `DEVBIN_GATE_FLAGS` is passed at `lib/gatecmd:141`, `lib/gatecmd:162` and `lib/resolve:777`. The command-level gate at `lib/resolve:909-915` (run_command's sealed branch) calls neither and appends raw `"$@"` after `--`. It was added later (WP-14), and the comment promising no drift was never re-read against it. **A Highlander claim written as a promise rather than as a test is how the third site got in unnoticed.**

The comment above the site is false on the same term: `lib/resolve:894` says a command-level gate "seals on exactly the terms an option-level one does (D19)".

## Fix shape

- `gate_split_args "$@"` at the command-level site, with `DEVBIN_GATE_FLAGS` before `--` and `DEVBIN_GATE_ARGS` after it, exactly as run_option does.
- A behavioural arm per flag at the command-level gate, driven red first.
- A class arm: every gate site that forwards user argv to `run_gate` routes it through `gate_split_args`, so a fourth site cannot repeat this.
- The D19 comment and gate_split_args' header corrected to name every site, or better, to point at the arm rather than enumerate.

## Routing

hv ruled 2026-09-18: fix before the fleet sweep, since the sweep is the propagation event. vc builds, dc reviews. `lib/resolve` and `lib/runlog` are vendored, so this goes in the sweep's pre-notice.


## Closed

**Built** at `860afd3` (the command-level site through `gate_split_args`, four behavioural arms, a class arm, the D19 comment rewritten to point at the arms) and **round two** at `9196ca3`, after dc's review found two holes in the class arm: the raw-argv regex missed the braced `${@}` and `${@:n}`, and `gate_spans` ended a span at the `--` line, so argv continued below it was never read. `gate_spans` now reads a call to its last line and prints flags and argv as separate fields, so 0085's `--source` check cannot be satisfied by a tool argument spelled `--source`.

**dc's verdict on round two: OK, with one gap** (scratch copies of `3c22861`). Every mutant at the `@builtin` opener was killed, but by the class arm alone: the four behavioural arms drive the command-level gate, so no behavioural arm reached the two catalogue openers. dc's own mutant -- argv laundered through a local array, `local -a _raw=("$@")` then ARGS plus `"${_raw[@]}"` -- passed every suite, because a lexical reader cannot follow a copy.

**The gap, closed**: two arms in `dispatch.bats` run the real `run_builtin_gate` and the real `run_gate` in-process with only the catalogue readers stubbed, one per catalogue opener (`@builtin` function, catalogue command line), each asserting that `--purge` purges a prior pair and that only the ordinary argument reaches the tool. Against six mutants (raw argv in place of ARGS, the array launder, FLAGS dropped -- at each of the two sites), each is killed by its own site's arm and by no other. dispatch 86/0; no new shellcheck findings.

**What still holds a future site**: the class arm, which finds a new `run_gate` opener lexically, and a site arm that the new opener would need. A launder at a site with no behavioural arm is invisible, which is the reason each site has one.
